title: Right-decalage last-vertex cocone and augmentation comparison prism
statement: Use nerves, quasicategories and coherent transformations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\Delta_+$, $\Delta$, $D$, $i$, $j$ and $U$ be the explicit finite-ordinal categories and functors of [lem-coef-right-decalage-index-calculus], in a fixed universe. Put $s=Uj:\Delta_+\to\Delta$ and let $q:\Delta\hookrightarrow\Delta_+$ be inclusion. The inclusions of original elements define a natural transformation $\eta:\operatorname{id}_{\Delta_+}\to qs$. The inclusions of the last element define a natural transformation $\lambda:\operatorname{const}_{\{\infty\}}\to U$. For any quasicategory $\mathcal C$ and coherent functor $\overline Z:N(\Delta_+)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$, set $Z=\overline ZN(q^{\mathrm{op}})$ and $F=ZN(U^{\mathrm{op}})$. The prism obtained by applying $Z$ to $N(\lambda^{\mathrm{op}})$ is the cocone $a:F\to\operatorname{const}_{Z_0}$ induced by the unique-arrow transformation to $\varnothing$ in $D^{\mathrm{op}}$; its component at $\varnothing$ is $1_{Z_0}$. Its restriction along $N(j^{\mathrm{op}})$ augments the right shift $H_n=Z_{n+1}$ by restriction to the last vertex. The prism obtained by applying $\overline Z$ to $N(\eta^{\mathrm{op}})$ is a coherent transformation $FN(j^{\mathrm{op}})\to\overline Z$. Its restriction to nonempty ordinals is restriction from $Z_{n+1}$ to the first $n+1$ vertices; its component at $\varnothing$ is the original augmentation $Z_0\to\overline Z(\varnothing)$. These identifications are of the whole nerve prisms, including all higher simplices. No groupoid, realization or colimit assertion is assumed or concluded.

source.place: HTT Lemma 6.1.3.17 and proof of Proposition 6.1.3.19 (printed pp.554–556): right shift, last-vertex augmentation and the evident augmented transformation; full nerve-prism identification stated explicitly. No Stacks tag states this quasicategory-valued identification.

proof.text: For an ordinal $J$ write $J^+=J\sqcup\{\infty\}$. By [lem-coef-right-decalage-index-calculus], $sJ=J^+$ and $s(f)=f^+$, where $f^+$ agrees with $f$ on $J$ and fixes the new last element. Let $e_J:J\to J^+$ be inclusion. It is monotone, including for $J=\varnothing$. For every monotone $f:J\to K$, both $f^+e_J$ and $e_Kf$ send $x\in J$ to $f(x)$. Thus these maps are equal, even when $J$ is empty, and $e_J$ defines the asserted $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{\Delta_+}\Rightarrow qs$.

source.place: Lecture II, Definitions 2.1–2.2, printed pp.13–14, for nerve and functor simplicial sets; the explicit ordinal and prism calculation is by Q27, not a theorem quoted from the notes.

proof.text: For $J\in D$ let $l_J:\{\infty\}\to UJ$ select the new last element. For an arrow $g:J\to K$ of $D$, its underlying map fixes that element, so $U(g)l_J=l_K$. This proves naturality of $\lambda$. The unique arrow $r_J:\varnothing\to J$ in $D$ is exactly the last-element inclusion on the underlying singleton; hence $U(r_J)=l_J$. Also $r_{\varnothing}=1_{\varnothing}$ and $g r_J=r_K$, since both sides send the singleton to the last element. Taking opposites gives $t:\mathrm{id}_{D^{\mathrm{op}}}\Rightarrow\operatorname{const}_{\varnothing}$, with $U^{\mathrm{op}}t=\lambda^{\mathrm{op}}$ on objects and arrows.

source.place: Lecture II, Definitions 2.1–2.2, printed pp.13–14, for nerve and functor simplicial sets; the explicit ordinal and prism calculation is by Q27, not a theorem quoted from the notes.

proof.text: Use the nerve and coherent-transformation definitions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Explicitly, for $b:P\Rightarrow Q$ between ordinary functors $I\to A$, its prism is the nerve of the functor $T_b:I\times[1]\to A$. This sends $(x,0)$ to $Px$ and $(x,1)$ to $Qx$, uses $P(f),Q(f)$ on same-level arrows, and sends a mixed arrow over $f:x\to y$ to $Q(f)b_x=b_yP(f)$. For a composable pair at levels $0,0,1$, composition gives $b_zP(g)P(f)=b_zP(gf)$; at levels $0,1,1$ it gives $Q(g)Q(f)b_x=Q(gf)b_x$; constant levels use functoriality. Identities follow from those of $P,Q$. An $m$-simplex of $N(I)\times\Delta^1$ is a pair $\sigma:[m]\to I$, $\epsilon:[m]\to[1]$, equivalently the functor $(\sigma,\epsilon)$ into the product. Send it to $T_b(\sigma,\epsilon)$. Restriction along every $\theta:[r]\to[m]$ commutes with this formula by composition of functors, proving directly that it is a simplicial map. Its endpoints are $NP,NQ$. Postcomposition with any simplicial map $W:N(A)\to\mathcal C$ therefore gives the coherent transformation with components $W(b_x)$, by the displayed definition of $\operatorname{Fun}(-,\mathcal C)_1$.

source.place: Lecture II, Definitions 2.1–2.2, printed pp.13–14, for nerve and functor simplicial sets; the explicit ordinal and prism calculation is by Q27, not a theorem quoted from the notes.

proof.text: Apply step 3 to $\lambda^{\mathrm{op}}:U^{\mathrm{op}}\Rightarrow\operatorname{const}_{\{\infty\}}$ and postcompose with $Z$. Its endpoints are $F$ and $\operatorname{const}_{Z_0}$, so this is a cocone in the definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Step 2 identifies the ordinary transformations $U^{\mathrm{op}}t$ and $\lambda^{\mathrm{op}}$. Their interval functors agree at both levels and on every mixed arrow: both use $U^{\mathrm{op}}(t_y\circ f)=U^{\mathrm{op}}(t_y)U^{\mathrm{op}}(f)$ over $f:x\to y$ in $D^{\mathrm{op}}$. Hence their nerves agree on each pair $(\sigma,\epsilon)$ of step 3. Postcomposition with $Z$ identifies the whole cocone prism with the one induced by the unique arrows to $\varnothing$. At $\varnothing$, $l_{\varnothing}$ is the identity of the singleton. Its nerve edge is degenerate; $Z$ preserves degeneracies, so $a_{\varnothing}=1_{Z_0}$.

source.place: Lecture II, Definitions 2.1–2.2, printed pp.13–14, for nerve and functor simplicial sets; the explicit ordinal and prism calculation is by Q27, not a theorem quoted from the notes.

proof.text: Restrict this cocone along $N(j^{\mathrm{op}})$. Its diagram has value $Z(J^+)$ at $J$ and uses the maps $f^+$ of step 1 on operators. For nonempty $J=[n]$, this is $H_n=Z_{n+1}$ with every operator fixing the newly added last vertex. The restricted cocone leg is $Z(l_J^{\mathrm{op}})$, which is restriction to that last vertex. At the empty ordinal its value is $Z_0$ and its leg is the identity by step 4. This also identifies the augmentation encoded by the diagram on $\Delta_+^{\mathrm{op}}$: its arrow $J\to\varnothing$ is $j^{\mathrm{op}}$ of the unique empty-source map, whose image under $U$ selects the new last element. On all chains the same equality holds after composition with the indexing functors, so restricting the prism gives this augmentation together with all its simplices.

source.place: Lecture II, Definitions 2.1–2.2, printed pp.13–14, for nerve and functor simplicial sets; the explicit ordinal and prism calculation is by Q27, not a theorem quoted from the notes.

proof.text: Taking opposites in step 1 gives $\eta^{\mathrm{op}}:(qs)^{\mathrm{op}}\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}_{\Delta_+^{\mathrm{op}}}$. Its step-3 prism postcomposed with $\overline Z$ has source $\overline ZN((qs)^{\mathrm{op}})=ZN(s^{\mathrm{op}})=FN(j^{\mathrm{op}})$ and target $\overline Z$; these equalities hold on every chain because $s=Uj$ and $Z=\overline ZN(q^{\mathrm{op}})$. At nonempty $J=[n]$, its component is $\overline Z(e_J^{\mathrm{op}})$, hence restriction from $Z_{n+1}$ to the first $n+1$ vertices. At $J=\varnothing$, $e_J:\varnothing\to\{\infty\}$ is the original augmentation arrow, so the component is exactly $Z_0\to\overline Z(\varnothing)$. For every $(\sigma,\epsilon)$, the comparison is explicitly $\overline Z(T_{\eta^{\mathrm{op}}}(\sigma,\epsilon))$. Restriction to nonempty ordinals, to the empty vertex, or along a simplicial operator is precomposition of this same formula. Thus these are identifications of entire prisms, not merely their component edges. No horn-filling, realization or colimit theorem is used.
